description: A loan repayment is a deduction from net pay, not a statutory contribution. Year-end annualization read contributions by label text, so a repayment on 'SSS Salary Loan' or 'Pag-IBIG Multi-Purpose Loan' (the engine labels it 'Loan, <loan type>' under the code LOAN-<id>) was summed as an SSS or Pag-IBIG contribution. Contributions are a non-taxable bucket, so every repayment lowered taxable income and inflated the year-end refund. Phase 24 certifies the corrected behaviour with three workers hired at the switch on the same salary: a control with no loan, a worker repaying an SSS Salary Loan, and a worker repaying a Pag-IBIG Multi-Purpose Loan and a company loan. Both loan workers' year-end settlement must equal the control's.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (up to 10,417 exempt; 10,417 to 16,667: 15%; 16,667 to 33,333: 937.50 + 20%; over 33,333: 4,270.70 + 25% of the excess); annual table (up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000 to 400,000: 15% of the excess over 250,000). Only the employee's mandatory SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions are excluded from taxable compensation; a loan repayment is the employee's own money used to settle a debt and is not such a contribution (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(f)).
sources.thirteenthMonth: Presidential Decree 851: 13th month pay = one twelfth of basic salary earned in the year; exempt up to 90,000 together with other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)).

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing, monthly salary 60,000 (30,000 a cutoff), every worker hired 2026-07-01 so only the 12 engine cutoffs 13-24 exist and there are no imported rows. An ordinary cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 100 (1,725); taxable 30,000 - 1,725 = 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 0.20 x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10. Loan repayments are taken from net pay after tax, so they change net pay and nothing else in the cutoff.
Each loan is active with a remaining balance equal to twelve repayments, so the full cutoff deduction is taken in every cutoff 13-24 and the balance is never the limit.

Year end for a worker with no 13th month paid: entries 12 x 30,000; entitlement = basic earned 360,000 / 12 = 30,000 is accrued unpaid and added to gross compensation; contributions 12 x 1,725 = 20,700 and ONLY those; the 30,000 sits inside the 90,000 pool; non-taxable = exempt pool + contributions; taxable = gross - non-taxable; tax = 15% x (taxable - 250,000); withheld = the sum of the WHT lines only; a refund is a negative adjustment.

noLoanControl.description: No loan. Net pay 25,015.90 in every cutoff. Year end: gross 360,000 + 30,000 accrued = 390,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 = 50,700; taxable 339,300; tax 15% x 89,300 = 13,395.00; withheld 12 x 3,259.10 = 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20.

sssSalaryLoan.description: An 'SSS Salary Loan' repaid 500.00 a cutoff (6,000.00 over the 12 cutoffs). Cutoff net pay 25,015.90 - 500.00 = 24,515.90; gross, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and withholding are the control's. Year end must equal the control: statutory contributions 20,700 (NOT 26,700), non-taxable 50,700, taxable 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20. Before the fix the repayments counted as 6,000 of SSS contributions: non-taxable 56,700, taxable 333,300, tax 12,495.00 and a refund 900.00 too large (26,614.20).

pagibigAndCompanyLoans.description: A 'Pag-IBIG Multi-Purpose Loan (MPL)' repaid 400.00 a cutoff (4,800.00 over 12 cutoffs) and a 'Company Emergency Loan' repaid 250.00 a cutoff (3,000.00). Cutoff net pay 25,015.90 - 400.00 - 250.00 = 24,365.90. Year end must equal the control: contributions 20,700, taxable 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20. Before the fix the Pag-IBIG repayments counted as 4,800 of contributions: non-taxable 55,500, taxable 334,500, tax 12,675.00 and a refund 720.00 too large (26,434.20). The company loan never matched and must stay uncounted.

limitations: Only loan repayments are exercised end to end. An earned wage advance recovery (code EWA-) and a benefit plan deduction (code BEN-) are excluded by the same change and covered by unit tests on the line parser, not by a real-engine case here.
One salary, 'split' timing, a worker hired at the switch (no imported history), loans that are never limited by disposable pay.
Final pay (separation) reads contributions by exact code and is not affected by the label defect; it is not exercised here.
Year-end rows already computed under the old rule are replaced only when year end is recomputed; the stored rule version string is unchanged.
